name: Kato Poli
tagline: The lower town between the port and the square
description: The flat commercial grid running back from the ferry terminal, built around Georgiou Square and the arcaded streets that give central Patras its character. Shops, offices, the covered market and most of the city's services are here, along with the widest choice of flats and the shortest walk to everything.
bestFor: Anyone wanting the market, the square and the ferries all within walking distance
pros: Everything practical within a ten-minute walk
The best rental supply in the city
Arcaded streets that work in both sun and winter rain
cons: Some blocks are visibly run down
The area right by the terminal is less comfortable at night

name: Ano Poli
tagline: The upper town below the castle, reached by the stairs
description: The old quarter climbing the hill behind the centre, reached by long flights of steps and holding the Byzantine castle, the Roman odeon and neoclassical houses in various states of repair. It is quieter, cooler in summer and has the only real views in Patras, over the gulf towards the bridge.
bestFor: Stays that want views, quiet and the historic quarter, and do not mind stairs
pros: Views over the gulf and the Rio bridge
Castle grounds and the odeon on the doorstep
Noticeably cooler and quieter than the lower town
cons: The stairs are a genuine daily commitment
Few shops, and none of them large

name: Psila Alonia and the University Side
tagline: Student streets, the bars and the cheapest rents
description: The area around Psila Alonia square and the streets running towards the university quarter, where the student bars on Riga Feraiou and Agiou Nikolaou concentrate. Rents are low because the market is built for students, and the nightlife is the best and cheapest in the city.
bestFor: Long stays on a budget with the bars at the end of the street
pros: Ten minutes on foot to the square

name: Agyia and the Northern Seafront
tagline: The coast road north, with the beach and quieter blocks
description: The residential strip running northeast along the gulf towards Rio, with a long seafront promenade, swimming spots and newer apartment blocks facing the water. It is calmer than the centre, has sea views for not much more money and is twenty minutes on foot or a short bus ride into town.
bestFor: Longer stays that want to swim before work and a quieter street at night
pros: Sea swimming and a long promenade
cons: Twenty to twenty-five minutes to the square
The coast road carries steady traffic

name: Rio
tagline: The bridge end, the university campus and the ferries to Antirrio
description: A separate settlement eight kilometres northeast where the main University of Patras campus sits beside the enormous cable-stayed bridge across the gulf. It has student housing, a beach, a small castle and its own restaurants, and it functions as a university town attached to the city rather than a suburb.
bestFor: Anyone whose reason to be here is the university, with a beach thrown in
pros: University campus and its facilities on the doorstep
cons: Twenty-five minutes by bus into central Patras
